subject: RivetPay post-call: TCO recap, batching/cache levers & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@rivetpay.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@rivetpay.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: RivetPay post-call: TCO recap, batching/cache levers & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific asks we can follow up on: 

Summary of pain points
- High token spend on customer-facing flows (KYC + chat), spikes during peak hours causing both cost and latency issues.
- Current hosting has limited batching; engineering resource constraints to build an in-house caching layer.
- Procurement needs a clear cost/benefit case for pilot vs. full rollout (30–90 day timeline).

Goals we heard
- Reduce monthly inference spend by 30–50% while keeping average p99 latency under 400ms for chat flows.
- Validate a pilot that demonstrates unit-cost improvements and operational simplicity.

Key levers we discussed
- Batching: combining short requests during peak windows to improve GPU utilization.
- KV/prefix cache: caching stable prompt prefixes (transactions, product text) to avoid re-computation.
- Model selection & quantization: a cost-accuracy tradeoff path (fast variant for low-cost surface, higher-quality for risky flows).

Immediate asks / data we need to size an accurate TCO:
1) Monthly active users (MAU) and estimated requests/day for the chat + KYC pipelines.
2) Example request profiles: average tokens per request (input + output) and 95th/99th percentiles.
3) Any existing SLOs you must meet (latency, availability) and procurement budget target for the pilot.

Next steps (proposed)
- We’ll share our TCO workbook (RWC TCO workbook) with a baseline and two pilot scenarios (conservative / aggressive).
- You share anonymized usage sample and the MAU estimate — that lets us run concrete token-econ outcomes.
- Align on decision date — you mentioned end of Q4 tentatively.

I’ve copied Ben Carter (pricing & pilot packaging) to help with illustrative pilot pricing and potential credit offsets. I’ll attach the TCO workbook and an example cost-model after we get the usage sample.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none in this message
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@rivetpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@rivetpay.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RivetPay post-call: TCO recap, batching/cache levers & next steps

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Couple clarifications from our side: 

Data points you asked for
- MAU (chat + KYC): ~120k monthly active users across US and EU, with ~1.8M requests/month combined today.
- Token profile (rough): median 420 tokens/request, mean 580 tokens/request, 95th ~1,400, spikes up to 4,000 for long transcripts.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 < 300ms for chat flows; KYC can tolerate higher latency (p95 < 1s).
- Budget: procurement has given guidance of $35k–$45k/mo for pilot validation; any sustained production spend will need internal approvals beyond that.

Attached a small extract of our usage logs (anonymized) and our security questionnaire answers. We redact user IDs but left timestamps and token counts.

Decision timeline
- We’re targeting a pilot decision by 2026-11-30, internal procurement sign-off by end of Q4 if pilot looks good.

If you can run a baseline TCO with these numbers and show a 30%+ unit-cost improvement using batching + cache, we’ll prioritize engineering time to provide sample logs.

—Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, RivetPay
alex.torres@rivetpay.com

Attachments: usage_report_q2.csv, rivetpay-security-answers.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@rivetpay.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@rivetpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RivetPay post-call: TCO recap, batching/cache levers & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the data. That token distribution is helpful and confirms there’s room for caching and batching wins (especially on repeated prompt prefixes and the long-transcript tail).

What we’ll do next (quick timeline):
- Today: I’ll run your CSV through our RWC TCO workbook and return two modeled scenarios: 
  • Pilot (30-day, constrained): conservative batching assumptions, no model quantization changes.
  • Pilot+Ops (90-day): more aggressive batching and a KV cache on the hottest prefixes; shows the operational uplift and unit-cost delta.
- Request: If you can provide one-week of raw (anonymized) request logs in the same format, we’ll include per-hour batching sensitivity.
- Deliverable: TCO workbook + short one-page ROI summary and recommended pilot success metrics (cost per 1k requests, latency p95, cache hit rate).

Attaching the RWC TCO workbook — fill the highlighted cells if you want to tweak assumptions. Ben — can you propose two pilot pricing options (pilot credit + reserved burst pricing vs pay-as-you-go w/ committed discount)?

Thanks —
Soojin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: rwc_tco_workbook.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@rivetpay.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T10:43:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing options for RivetPay pilot (2 quick buckets)

Alex / Soojin — looping in proposed commercial structures so Alex has concrete numbers to show procurement. Two straightforward options: 

Option A — Pilot Credit + Measured Usage
- 30-day pilot, $30k credit applied to platform usage.
- If usage exceeds credits, overage billed at pay-as-you-go rates with a 10% pilot discount.
- Includes one week of prioritized onboarding & a lite packet of Ops runbooks.
- No long-term commitment required; we’ll capture metrics and propose a production commitment once pilot KPIs are met.

Option B — Committed Discount (short-term reserved)
- 3-month reserved commit of $40k/mo (billed monthly) with a 20% unit-cost reduction vs standard hosted rates.
- Includes priority capacity during peak windows and an agreed fallback policy.
- Pilot credits of $10k applied up front for onboarding.

Quick ROI framing (from our model)
- With your numbers and conservative batching + a small KV cache, we estimate a 28–35% reduction in token-driven spend under Option B at the 90-day mark. Option A typically shows 18–22% in 30 days as we tune batching.

Next actions
- If either looks interesting, confirm which option to put in a one-page SOW.
- Alex — we can also run a short test on a 48-hour sample to validate the cache hit-rate assumptions before committing.

—Ben Carter
Sr. Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
